\title{Sixfold and sevenfold rotationally symmetric point sets\\ without a convex octagon}
\author{[author]}
\date{Draft P1, 6 November 2026. Not refereed.}

\begin{document}
\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
Let $ES(k)$ be the least $n$ such that every $n$ points in general position in the plane contain $k$ points in convex
position. Erd\H{o}s and Szekeres conjectured $ES(k)=2^{k-2}+1$; this is known for $k\le6$ and open for $k=7$ and $k=8$.
We study point sets that are invariant under a rotation of order $m$. For $k=8$ we show that the largest $m$-fold
rotationally symmetric set in general position with no $8$ points in convex position has exactly $60$ points for $m=6$
and exactly $64$ points for $m=7$. Sixfold symmetric sets in general position have $6t$ points (or consist of the centre
alone) and sevenfold ones $7t$ or $7t+1$, so this says that $ES(8)=65$ holds within these two symmetry classes and that
the largest sizes it permits there are attained. The proof is computer-assisted. A reduction checked in Lean~4 brings
the upper bounds down to invariant sets of exactly $66$, resp.\ $70$, points without the centre; by a layer lemma
(Lean-checked core, written assembly) these are $11$ nested regular hexagons, resp.\ $10$ nested regular heptagons,
in general position without a convex octagon. Two separately implemented encoders turn these statements into CNF
formulas; the soundness of the
encodings is a written proof (not refereed), and the formulas are refuted by CaDiCaL with LRAT proofs accepted by the
verified checker \cakelpr{}. For the sixfold bound, a hash-bound \cakelpr{} replay (6 November 2026) solved all $64$
cube formulas again, after regenerating them with hashes matching the record, and \cakelpr{} accepted every fresh
proof. The lower
bounds are explicit sets with coordinates in $\mathbb Z[\zeta_6]$ and $\mathbb Z[\zeta_7]$, five sixfold and seven
sevenfold order types, checked by exact computation with separately written programs. Every statement carries a rigor
label. The half-turn and the threefold, fourfold and fivefold cases remain open.
\end{abstract}

\tableofcontents

%======================================================================================================================
\section{Introduction}\label{sec:intro}

\paragraph{The problem.} Let $ES(k)$ be the least $n$ such that every set of $n$ points in general position in the
plane contains $k$ points in convex position. Erd\H{o}s and Szekeres proved that $ES(k)$ exists~\cite{ES35}, constructed
$2^{k-2}$ points in general position without $k$ points in convex position~\cite{ES61}, and conjectured
$ES(k)=2^{k-2}+1$. The conjecture holds for $k\le6$: $ES(4)=5$ (E.~Klein, see~\cite{ES35}), $ES(5)=9$ (Makai and
Tur\'an, unpublished, as reported in~\cite{ES61}; published proof by Kalbfleisch, Kalbfleisch and Stanton~\cite{KKS70}) and
$ES(6)=17$, proved by Szekeres and Peters with a computer search~\cite{SP06} (a formally verified reduction is due to
Mari\'c~\cite{Mar19}, and Heule and Scheucher re-proved it by SAT~\cite{HS24}). It is open for $k=7$ and $k=8$. The best
refereed upper bound for $k=8$ that we know of is $ES(8)\le408$~\cite{MV16}. Unrefereed bounds are $ES(8)\le319$ in
Schroeder's preprint~\cite{Sch26} and $ES(8)\le311$ in separate work of this project, which is checked by the Lean kernel
in a single run and built on Schroeder's omission method and catalogs (\dirn{NOVELTY20261106}). Asymptotically $ES(k)=2^{k+o(k)}$
by Suk~\cite{Suk17}, with an improved error term in~\cite{HMPT20}.

\paragraph{Symmetric point sets.} Imposing a symmetry shrinks the search space, and optimality may be easier to prove
for structured sets. Subercaseaux, Mackey, Qian and Heule (SMQH)~\cite{SMQH25} built rotational symmetry into SAT
encodings, combined them with a local-search realizer, and found fourfold and fivefold symmetric $16$-point sets without
a convex hexagon~\cite[\S6.1, App.~C]{SMQH25} (see also Mackey's thesis~\cite{Mac25}); for $32$ points without a convex
heptagon they report that no realizable fourfold symmetric set exists~\cite[\S6.2]{SMQH25}. They wrote~\cite[\S7]{SMQH25}:
``for the Erd\H{o}s--Szekeres problem, we suspect that there are symmetric constructions for all $k\ge7$, and proving
this could represent progress toward the conjectured bound $g(k)=2^{k-2}+1$, since it might be easier to prove optimality
for more structured solutions.'' Their results stop at $k=7$. This paper treats $k=8$ for the two rotation orders for
which we could settle both directions, $m=6$ and $m=7$.

\paragraph{Results.} For $m\ge2$ and $k\ge3$ let $\Nrot{m}{k}$ be the largest number of points of a finite set in
general position in the plane that is invariant under the rotation by $2\pi/m$ about some point and contains no $k$
points in convex position.

\begin{theorem}[main theorem; rigor as stated below]\label{thm:main}
$\Nrot{6}{8}=60$ and $\Nrot{7}{8}=64$. In detail:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item \emph{(upper bounds)} every set of at least $61$ points in general position that is invariant under a rotation
by $2\pi/6$ contains $8$ points in convex position, and so does every set of at least $65$ points in general position
that is invariant under a rotation by $2\pi/7$;
\item \emph{(lower bounds)} there are sixfold symmetric sets of $60$ points (ten nested regular hexagons) and
sevenfold symmetric sets of $64$ points (nine nested regular heptagons and the centre) in general position without $8$
points in convex position; they include at least five, resp.\ seven, pairwise different order types.
\end{enumerate}
\emph{Rigor.} Part~(a) is computer-assisted: unsatisfiability certificates (\cakelpr) for two separately implemented
encoders (Section~\ref{sec:cert}). For $m=7$ both certificates were replayed against regenerated formulas with matching
hashes. For $m=6$ all $64$ cube formulas were regenerated with matching hashes, solved again and certified in a
hash-bound \cakelpr{} replay (6 November 2026), $64$ of $64$ accepted. This rests on a Lean-checked reduction
(Section~\ref{sec:layer}) and a written soundness proof of the encodings, not refereed (Section~\ref{k8s:sec}), whose
remaining gaps are listed as (G1)--(G4) in Section~\ref{k8s:sec:trust}. Part~(b) is exact computation
(Section~\ref{sec:lower}).
\end{theorem}

\begin{corollary}[$ES(8)=65$ within two symmetry classes]\label{cor:es8}
Every set of at least $65$ points in general position that is invariant under a rotation of order $6$ or $7$ contains
$8$ points in convex position. For $m=6$ the largest size below $65$ that an $m$-fold symmetric set in general position
can have is $60$, for $m=7$ it is $64$, and both sizes are attained by sets without $8$ points in convex position.
(Rigor: Theorem~\ref{thm:main} together with the short argument below, a written proof, not refereed, which is new in
this draft and has had no internal review.)
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}[Proof (written proof, not refereed; new)]
A rotation $\rho'$ of order $m$ about a point $O$ is the rotation by $2\pi j/m$ about $O$ for some $j$ with
$\gcd(j,m)=1$. If $jj'\equiv1\pmod m$, then $\rho'^{\,j'}$ is the rotation $\rho$ by $2\pi/m$ about $O$, and a set
invariant under $\rho'$ is invariant under all powers of $\rho'$, so under $\rho$; Theorem~\ref{thm:main} applies.
A set invariant under $\rho$ is a union of $\rho$-orbits, each of $m$ points except the centre
$O$. If $m$ is even and the set is in general position and contains a point $p\ne O$, it does not contain $O$, since
$p$, $O$ and $\rho^{m/2}p=2O-p$ are collinear (Lean-checked, \lean{centre_not_mem_of_even};
Lemma~\ref{k8s:lem:centre}). So sixfold sets in general position have $6t$ points (or are $\{O\}$), and sevenfold ones
$7t$ or $7t+1$. The largest such numbers below $65$ are $60$ and $64=7\cdot9+1$. The rest is Theorem~\ref{thm:main}.
\end{proof}

So $\Nrot{6}{8}=60$ is not a separate phenomenon: $60$ is the largest multiple of $6$ below $65$, and the content of the
sixfold statement is the sixfold case of $ES(8)=65$ together with attainment. The same holds for $m=7$ and $64$.

\begin{remark}[affine symmetries; written proof (not refereed), new in this draft]\label{rem:affine}
The same values hold for sets invariant under an affine bijection $g$ of order $6$, resp.\ $7$. Indeed $g$ permutes the
set, which contains three non-collinear points, so a power of $g$ fixes three non-collinear points and is the identity;
averaging a scalar product over the finite group $\langle g\rangle$ gives a linear map $T$ with $\det T>0$ such that
$TgT^{-1}$ is a Euclidean isometry of the same order. An isometry of finite order at least $3$ is a rotation by
$2\pi j/m$ with $\gcd(j,m)=1$, whose powers include the rotation by $2\pi/m$, and $T$ preserves general position and
convex position. The conjugation of an affine symmetry to an isometry is Lean-checked inside
\lean{hasConvexNGon_of_affine_symmetry} (\dirn{SYMLEAN/AffineReduction.lean}~\cite{Supp}), but the statement of that
theorem quantifies over all non-identity Euclidean isometries and does not track the order of the symmetry; an
order-preserving version, which this remark needs, is not formalized.
\end{remark}

\paragraph{Method.} For $m\ge3$ and $K\le2m$, the convex layers of an $m$-fold symmetric set in general position
without $K$ points in convex position are regular $m$-gons about the centre, strictly nested (the \emph{layer lemma},
Lemma~\ref{lem:layer}, whose core is Lean-checked and whose assembly into layers is a written step; for $16$ points,
fourfold symmetry and $K=6$ this is the special case used by SMQH~\cite[\S3.2]{SMQH25}). The reduction of part~(a) of
Theorem~\ref{thm:main} to two statements about invariant sets of exactly $66$ and exactly $70$ points without the centre
(\lean{Sixfold66} and \lean{Sevenfold70}, Proposition~\ref{prop:reduction}) is Lean-checked; that such sets are $11$
nested regular hexagons, resp.\ $10$ nested regular heptagons, is Lemma~\ref{k8s:lem:layer} (Lean-checked core, written
assembly). The orientation of
a triple of points of such a configuration is determined, in many cases, by the circular order of the directions of the
points and their antipodes, which depends only on the relative phases of the layers; together with nesting facts and a
clause family that forbids convex octagons through chains around a pivot, this gives a CNF formula
(Section~\ref{sec:enc}). Section~\ref{k8s:sec} proves that every real configuration yields a model; the formulas are
refuted with LRAT proofs checked by \cakelpr{} (Section~\ref{sec:cert}). The lower bounds were found by search
(alternating projections between real configurations and SAT models, a phase-fixed linear-programming loop, simulated
annealing and cluster constructions) and are verified in exact arithmetic (Section~\ref{sec:lower}).

\paragraph{What is and is not claimed.} The theorem is computer-assisted and has not been refereed. Its weakest links
are the written parts of the soundness argument, in particular that the Python generators emit exactly the analysed
clause families (gap~(G1) of Section~\ref{k8s:sec:trust}). Every \cakelpr{} verdict that the upper bounds use is bound
to the hashes of its formula and proof files (Section~\ref{sec:cert}). The proof files are archived outside the repository and
are not yet public. No statement here is a priority claim.

\subsection{Related work and credit}\label{sec:related}

\paragraph{Computer-assisted Erd\H{o}s--Szekeres-type results.} Besides the works cited above~\cite{SP06,Mar19,HS24}, Balko and Valtr ran a
SAT attack on the Erd\H{o}s--Tuza--Valtr refinement of the conjecture~\cite{BV17}; Subercaseaux et al.\ verified the
encoding of the empty hexagon theorem in Lean~4 and checked its proof with \cakelpr~\cite{SNGCCH24}, a precedent for
the combination of Lean and verified proof checking used here (our encoder soundness is only partly formalized);
Krapivin, Przybocki and Heule study satisfiability modulo realizability~\cite{KPH26}; and Dumitru reports SAT
computations for the $33$-point problem ($k=7$) on anchored subfamilies~\cite{Dum25}. One of Dumitru's convex-layer
templates implies the fivefold case of the analogous statement for $k=7$, with priority~\cite[\S7, Table~1]{Dum25}; we
found no statement on symmetric sets for $k\ge8$ in~\cite{Dum25}. Georgiev, G\'omez-Serrano, Tao and Wagner give
$2^{k-2}$-point sets without a convex $k$-gon for $k\le8$, with no symmetry stated~\cite[\S38]{GGTW25}.

\paragraph{Symmetric sets.} Rotational symmetry in SAT encodings for Erd\H{o}s--Szekeres-type problems, and the special
case of the layer lemma noted above, are due to SMQH~\cite{SMQH25} and Mackey~\cite{Mac25}; our encodings likewise
build the rotation into the variables, with one variable per rotation orbit of triples. For the other symmetry types at $k=8$ the following is known to
us. For reflections, the largest octagon-free set has $46$ points; this follows by an elementary mirror lemma, as shown
in a companion note~\cite[\dirn{WRITEUP/note/symmetric_extremal.tex}]{Supp}, from Baek's theorem~\cite[Thm.~1.6]{Bae25}
that every set of $\binom{n-1}{2}+2$ points in general position with distinct $x$-coordinates contains a $4$-cap (four
points with increasing $x$-coordinates and decreasing slopes) or $n$ points in convex position. For the half-turn, Baek and Balko's blow-up
lemma~\cite[Lemma~14]{BB25} applied to the $16$-point sets of~\cite{SMQH25,Mac25} gives $64$-point centrally symmetric
octagon-free sets (same note). These are not results of this paper.

\paragraph{What we did not find.} In the sources we inspected we did not find prior work on rotationally symmetric
point sets without $8$ points in convex position, or on the values $\Nrot{6}{8}$ and $\Nrot{7}{8}$. The inspection
covered SMQH~\cite{SMQH25} (arXiv version~1; the CICM chapter text was not accessed), Mackey's
thesis~\cite{Mac25}, \cite{Dum25,GGTW25,KPH26,KK26,Bae25,BB25}, the survey~\cite{MS00}, arXiv listings and full-text
searches, Zenodo, GitHub and general web searches on 1--2, 3, 4 and 6 November 2026 (records:
\dirn{LIT}, \dirn{NOVELTY20261106}, \dirn{C6C7REVIEW/LITERATURE.md}~\cite{Supp}). The symmetric literature we found
stops at $k=7$. A bounded search can miss work, in particular journal versions, manuscripts and non-English sources; this
is not a priority claim.

\section{Definitions, notation and rigor labels}\label{sec:defs}

Points are elements of $\mathbb R^2$. For points $p,q,r$ let
\[
\orient(p,q,r)=(x_q-x_p)(y_r-y_p)-(y_q-y_p)(x_r-x_p),
\]
twice the signed area of the triangle $pqr$; it is positive if $p,q,r$ turn counterclockwise. A finite set is in
\emph{general position} if no three of its points are collinear, and in \emph{convex position} if no point lies in the
convex hull of the others. For $K\ge3$ a set is \emph{$K$-free} if none of its $K$-element subsets is in convex
position; a \emph{convex $K$-gon} of a set is a $K$-subset in convex position. Let $O$ be the origin and $\rho=\rho_m$ the
counterclockwise rotation by $2\pi/m$ about $O$. A set $S$ is \emph{$m$-fold (rotationally) symmetric} if $\rho S=S$
after translating its centre to $O$; its \emph{orbits} are the sets $\{\rho^jx\}$, regular $m$-gons for $x\ne O$.
$\Nrot{m}{k}$ is defined in Section~\ref{sec:intro}.

\paragraph{Lean conventions.} In Lean a point is \texttt{Point = Fin 2 \(\to\) \(\mathbb R\)}; the predicates \lean{GeneralPosition},
\lean{ConvexPosition} (Mathlib's \lean{ConvexIndependent} of the inclusion) and \texttt{HasConvexNGon n S} are those of
the repository's \lean{ErdosSzekeres.Definitions}; \texttt{rotAbout c a} is the rotation by the angle $a$ about $c$, and
\texttt{Invariant f S} means $f(p)\in S$ for all $p\in S$. Section~\ref{k8s:sec:setting} relates these to the notions
above.

\paragraph{Rigor labels.} Every statement carries one of the following labels.
\begin{itemize}
\item \emph{Lean-checked}: compiled with Lean~4.24.0~\cite{Lean4} and Mathlib~\cite{Mathlib} at commit
\texttt{f897ebcf}, with no \texttt{sorry}, \texttt{admit} or added axioms; \texttt{\#print axioms} reports only
\lean{propext}, \lean{Classical.choice} and \lean{Quot.sound}.
\item \emph{Certificate}: unsatisfiability of a specific CNF file, established by an LRAT proof~\cite{LRAT17} that the
verified checker \cakelpr~\cite{CakeLPR} accepted with the line \texttt{s VERIFIED UNSAT}. The solver
(CaDiCaL~3.0.1~\cite{CaDiCaL}, and 2.1.3 for the re-checks of 5 November and the sixfold
replay of 6 November) is not trusted. Acceptance by \lratcheck{} alone is not a certificate: the
\lratcheck{} of drat-trim at commit \texttt{2e3b2dc} accepts an invalid proof of a satisfiable formula unless
patched, a publicly known defect~\cite{DT} (our reproduction: \dirn{LRATCHECK20261105}), so its verdicts are cited as
supporting only. Where a \cakelpr{} verdict is on record only as a solve-time log line naming a cube label, without
formula or proof hashes, this is said each time it is mentioned; since the replay of 6 November the upper bounds do not
depend on such verdicts. A certificate proves a geometric statement only together
with the soundness of the encoding.
\item \emph{Exact computation}: integer or exact algebraic arithmetic on explicit data, by the programs named.
\item \emph{Written proof (not refereed)}: a complete written proof, here or in the supplementary material; where it
was internally reviewed, this is said.
\item \emph{Evidence only}: tests, timings and failed searches; never used as a proof.
\end{itemize}

\paragraph{Supplementary material.} Paths such as \dirn{C6UPPER} refer to directories under
\dirn{cloud/es7-2026-10-19/results} of the project repository~\cite{Supp}, which contain the programs, logs, point
sets, Lean files, hashes and reproduction commands. Proof files are in local archives outside the repository and are
not public; an archived public deposit of the supplementary material with a DOI is an open item of this draft.

\section{The layer reduction (Lean-checked core)}\label{sec:layer}

The Lean statements of this section are in \dirn{LAYERLEAN/LayerLemma.lean} (namespace
\lean{ErdosSzekeres.LayerLemma}); where a statement combines them by a written step, this is said.

\begin{lemma}[layer lemma; Lean-checked core (\lean{layers_are_orbits}, \lean{exists_layer}, \lean{strict_nesting},
\lean{centre_not_mem_of_even}); the assembly into layers is a written proof (not refereed)]\label{lem:layer}
Let $m\ge3$, $K\le2m$, and let $S$ be a finite $\rho$-invariant set in general position with no $K$ points in convex
position. Then $S\setminus\{O\}$ is the union of regular $m$-gons $L_0,L_1,\dots,L_{t-1}$ centred at $O$ (its convex
layers), and for $n<n'$, every vertex $x$ of $L_n$ and every $y\in L_{n'}$ satisfy $\orient(x,\rho x,y)>0$. If $m$ is
even and $S\ne\{O\}$, then $O\notin S$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
The set of hull vertices of $S\setminus\{O\}$ is $\rho$-invariant and nonempty, so it is a union of orbits of exactly
$m$ points each; two orbits would give $2m\ge K$ points in convex position, so it is one orbit, a regular $m$-gon. Peel
it off and repeat. For strict nesting, with $\tau=\pi/m$,
\[
\orient(x,\rho x,\rho^j x)=4\,|x-O|^2\sin\tau\,\sin j\tau\,\sin(j-1)\tau\ \ge0,
\]
so the vertices of a layer, and by convexity its hull, lie weakly to the left of each edge; equality would give three
collinear points of $S$. For even $m$, $\rho^{m/2}$ is the half-turn, and $p,O,2O-p$ are collinear.
\end{proof}

In Lean the core statement \lean{hullVerts_eq_orbitFS} is proved for an injective affine map whose points all have
minimal period $m$, without general position; \lean{hullVerts_eq_orbitFS_rotAbout} specialises it to rotations,
\lean{layers_are_orbits} and \lean{exists_layer} give the layers, \lean{card_peel} their sizes, \lean{strict_nesting}
the nesting (it needs general position and $m\ge2$), and \lean{centre_not_mem_of_even} the centre exclusion. Combining
these into the decomposition of $S\setminus\{O\}$ into layers $L_0,\dots,L_{t-1}$ is a short written step, not
formalized as one theorem. The version used by the soundness proof, for sets with exactly $mt$ points and their peeled
layers, is Lemma~\ref{k8s:lem:layer}; there the assembly is written out, and it is listed as unreviewed under
gap~(G4).

\paragraph{Polar form} (Lean-checked, \lean{orient_polar}). Writing the points as $O+r(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)$,
\[
\orient(a,b,d)=r_ar_b\sin(\theta_b-\theta_a)+r_br_d\sin(\theta_d-\theta_b)+r_dr_a\sin(\theta_a-\theta_d).
\]

\begin{lemma}[encoding facts; Lean-checked]\label{lem:facts}
Under the hypotheses of Lemma~\ref{lem:layer}:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item\emph{(rule A)} if the three angular gaps from $a$ to $b$ to $d$ lie in $(0,\pi)$, so that $O$ lies inside the
triangle, then $\orient(a,b,d)>0$ (\lean{orient_polar_centre_inside});
\item\emph{(rule B)} if $\theta_b=\theta_a+x$ and $\theta_d=\theta_b+y$ with $x,y>0$, $x+y<\pi$, and $r_b\ge
r_a,r_d$, then $\orient(a,b,d)>0$ (\lean{orient_polar_halfplane}, using $\sin x+\sin y>\sin(x+y)$,
\lean{sin_add_lt});
\item\emph{(radius order)} points of later layers are no farther from $O$ than points of earlier layers
(\lean{dist2_le_of_later});
\item\emph{(chains)} if $4\le K\le2m$, there are no pivot $p\in L_i$ and points $q_0,\dots,q_{K-2}$ of
$L_i\cup L_{i+1}\cup\cdots$, all other than $p$, with $\orient(p,q_s,q_{s+1})>0$ and $\orient(q_s,q_{s+1},q_{s+2})>0$
for all admissible $s$ (\lean{chain_clauses_sound});
\item\emph{(reduction)} if every $\rho$-invariant set in general position with exactly $mt$ points and without $O$ has
a convex $K$-gon, then so does every $\rho$-invariant set in general position with more than $m(t-1)$ points other than
$O$ (\lean{convexNGon_of_layers}).
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
(a)~All three sines are positive. (b)~By $r_b\ge r_a,r_d$ the polar form is at least
$r_ar_d(\sin x+\sin y-\sin(x+y))>0$. (c)~By convexity of the disc and Lemma~\ref{lem:layer}. (d)~\emph{Fan lemma}
(\lean{hasConvexNGon_of_fan}): a pivot and $n\ge3$ chain points in an open half-plane through the pivot, with all these
turns positive, are in convex position. \emph{Half-plane} (\lean{lin_pos_of_peel}): every other point of the layers
$\ge i$ lies strictly on the inner side of the tangent line at $p$; for $\rho^jp$ the value is
$|p-O|^2(1-\cos(2\pi j/m))$, and for later layers it follows from strict nesting at the two edges through $p$. So a chain
would be a convex $K$-gon. (e)~Peel $t$ layers of exactly $m$ points (\lean{card_peel}).
\end{proof}

The two statements that the certificates establish are, verbatim:
{\footnotesize
\begin{alltt}
def Sixfold66 : Prop :=
  \(\forall\) (T : Finset Point) (c : Point), GeneralPosition T \(\to\) c \(\notin\) T \(\to\)
    Invariant (rotAbout c (2 * Real.pi / 6)) T \(\to\) T.card = 66 \(\to\) HasConvexNGon 8 T
def Sevenfold70 : Prop :=
  \(\forall\) (T : Finset Point) (c : Point), GeneralPosition T \(\to\) c \(\notin\) T \(\to\)
    Invariant (rotAbout c (2 * Real.pi / 7)) T \(\to\) T.card = 70 \(\to\) HasConvexNGon 8 T
\end{alltt}}

\begin{proposition}[reduction; Lean-checked]\label{prop:reduction}
\lean{sixfold_octagon}: if \lean{Sixfold66} holds, then every set $S$ in general position with
\texttt{Invariant (rotAbout c (2 * Real.pi / 6)) S} and $|S|\ge61$ satisfies \texttt{HasConvexNGon 8 S}.
\lean{sevenfold_octagon}: if \lean{Sevenfold70} holds, the same holds with $2\pi/7$ and $|S|\ge65$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
For $m=6$ the centre is not in $S$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:layer}), so $|S|\ge61>6\cdot10$; for $m=7$, $|S\setminus\{c\}|\ge64>7\cdot9$.
Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:facts}(e) with $t=11$, resp.\ $t=10$. Lowering $61$ to $60$, resp.\ $65$ to $64$, makes the Lean
proof fail (\dirn{LAYERLEAN/README.md}).
\end{proof}

\paragraph{Build and axioms.} \dirn{LAYERLEAN/LayerLemma.lean} has SHA-256 \texttt{afb8542d\dots}
(Appendix~\ref{app:hashes}). It is checked with \verb|lake env lean| from the repository root (Lean~4.24.0, Mathlib
\texttt{f897ebcf}); the recorded run exits $0$ with no messages (\dirn{LAYERLEAN/logs/build.log}), and
\dirn{LAYERLEAN/logs/axioms.log} reports only \lean{propext}, \lean{Classical.choice}, \lean{Quot.sound} for every
theorem cited. For this draft the file was checked again on 6 November 2026 with the already-built dependencies and
$19$ \texttt{\#print axioms} lines appended (the declarations of Lemmas~\ref{lem:layer}, \ref{lem:facts} and
Proposition~\ref{prop:reduction}, among them \lean{fan_positive}): exit status $0$, the three standard axioms for all
$19$, $23$\,s wall clock and $2.6$\,GB peak memory.

\paragraph{What is not in Lean.} The assembly of the layer decomposition from the cited theorems
(Lemmas~\ref{lem:layer} and~\ref{k8s:lem:layer}), the classification of phase patterns (which of rules~A and~B applies,
and to which ordered triple), the perturbation to generic phases, the consistency of one variable per triple orbit, the
correspondence between the generator programs and the clause families, the reflection unit, the cube cover and the
passage from unsatisfiable DIMACS files to \lean{Sixfold66} and \lean{Sevenfold70}. These are the written proofs of
Section~\ref{k8s:sec}.

\section{The encodings}\label{sec:enc}

Fix $(m,K,t)$; the certified instances are $(6,8,11)$ and $(7,8,10)$. Label the points of $t$ nested regular $m$-gons
by $\Lambda=\{0,\dots,t-1\}\times\mathbb Z/m$, with layer $0$ outermost and $P(i,k)=r_i\,e(\theta_i+2\pi k/m)$,
$e(\varphi)=(\cos\varphi,\sin\varphi)$, and rotate so that $\theta_0=0$ (Definition~\ref{k8s:def:phase}). Let $u=\pi/m$
for odd $m$ and $u=2\pi/m$ for even $m$, and $\psi_i=\theta_i\bmod u$.

\paragraph{Variables.} (i)~One \emph{orientation variable} per rotation orbit of $3$-subsets of $\Lambda$, meaning
$\orient>0$ for a fixed representative ($7{,}634$ orbits at $(6,11)$, $7{,}820$ at $(7,10)$;
Lemma~\ref{k8s:lem:orbit}); (ii)~\emph{phase-order variables} $Y(i,j)=[\psi_i<\psi_j]$, $1\le i<j\le t-1$;
(iii)~for odd $m$, $H(i)=[\theta_i<\pi/m]$, $1\le i\le t-1$; (iv)~auxiliary \emph{chain variables}.

\paragraph{Clause families.}
\begin{itemize}
\item \emph{phase order}: the $Y$ variables form a strict total order (Lemma~\ref{k8s:lem:order});
\item \emph{angular}: for each triple orbit and each pattern of the phase order (and $H$ bits) of its layers, the
circular order of the three directions and their antipodes is determined; where rule~A or rule~B applies, the
orientation is fixed by a unit clause or by a clause conditional on the pattern (Lemma~\ref{k8s:lem:angB});
\item \emph{nesting}: $\orient(P(i,0),P(i,1),P(j,k))>0$ for $i<j$ (Lemma~\ref{k8s:lem:nestcl});
\item \emph{chains}: no chain of $K-1$ points around a pivot $(i,0)$ as in Lemma~\ref{lem:facts}(d)
(Lemma~\ref{k8s:lem:chain}). By rotation this covers every convex $K$-gon: take its outermost layer as $i$
(Remark~\ref{k8s:rem:complete}; not needed for soundness).
\end{itemize}
Even $m$ needs no $H$ variables, since antipodes are orbit points; a triple containing an antipodal pair of one layer
gets no angular clause, which is weaker but sound (Section~\ref{k8s:sec:antipodal}).

\paragraph{Two encoders.} \emph{Encoder A} is \dirn{C7UPPER/gen.py}; it classifies one sampled phase vector per pattern
in binary64 arithmetic and builds the chains forwards. \emph{Encoder B} is \dirn{C7UPPER/gen_b.py}, extended to even $m$
as \dirn{C6UPPER/encb/gen_b2.py}; it decides circular orders by exact integer comparisons, builds the chains backwards
and numbers the variables differently, and \dirn{gen_b2.py} reproduces the certified sevenfold formula of
\dirn{gen_b.py} byte for byte (exact computation). The two encoders share the written soundness argument, the canonical
triple representatives and part of the validation code, so they are separate implementations of one encoding, not
independent encodings. Section~\ref{k8s:sec} treats encoder~B as the primary object and encoder~A as a cross-check.

\paragraph{Symmetry breaking.} Besides $\theta_0=0$, a reflection in the $x$-axis maps a configuration to another one
with the same layers and reversed phase order (Lemma~\ref{k8s:lem:refl}), so the unit $Y(1,2)$ (even $m$) or $H(1)$ (odd
$m$) loses no generality. The sevenfold certificate of encoder~A uses $H(1)$; that of encoder~B uses no unit.

\paragraph{Instance sizes} (exact computation). At $(6,8,11)$ both encoders write $78{,}059$ variables and
$2{,}387{,}083$ clauses; by encoder~A's metadata (\dirn{C6UPPER/logs/regen.log}) $10{,}087$ of them are angular
($2{,}347$ units and $7{,}740$ conditional) and $2{,}376{,}426$ are chain clauses, and the remaining $570$ are the
$240=2\binom{10}{3}$ phase-order clauses and the $330=6\binom{11}{2}$ nesting units. At $(7,8,10)$ both write $80{,}080$
variables and $2{,}748{,}538$ clauses; $73{,}784$ are angular (\dirn{C7UPPER/README.md}), $315=7\binom{10}{2}$ are
nesting units and $168=2\binom{9}{3}$ phase-order clauses, which leaves $2{,}674{,}271$ chain clauses (by
subtraction).

\paragraph{Validation} (evidence only unless stated otherwise).
\begin{itemize}
\item \emph{Regeneration} (exact computation). Fresh runs of the generators reproduce the certified base formulas byte
for byte: the sixfold base formulas of both encoders and the three sevenfold formulas (A, A $+\,H(1)$, B) (hashes in
Appendix~\ref{app:hashes}; \dirn{C6UPPER/logs/regen.log}, \dirn{C6C7REVIEW/REPLAY.md}, \dirn{K8EXACT20261106}). All
$64$ sixfold cube files were regenerated on 6 November with \dirn{C6UPPER/tools/mkcubes.py}, and before any solving the
hash of each was found equal to its record in \dirn{C6UPPER/SHA256SUMS.txt}
(\dirn{C6UPPER/replay-2026-11-06}); the $6$ sampled on 4 November had already been regenerated with matching hashes
(\dirn{C6C7REVIEW/replay.json}). The cube sets used at solve time were checked structurally against the base-formula
hashes by \dirn{verify_cover.py} (\dirn{C6UPPER/logs/verify_cover.log}, \dirn{encb_verify_cover.log}), and the
regenerated ones by \dirn{verify_cover.py} (4 and 6 November) and \dirn{strict_cover.py} (4 November)
(Section~\ref{sec:cert}).
\item \emph{Real sets} (exact computation). The eight sevenfold $64$-point files of Section~\ref{sec:lower} and their
mirror images, with the centre removed, give $16$ configurations of $9$ nested heptagons; with the orientation and phase
variables computed exactly in $\mathbb Z[\zeta_7]$ and the chain variables at their least model, each satisfies all
$1{,}765{,}351$ clauses of both encoders' $9$-layer formulas, and exactly one of each set and its mirror satisfies
encoder~A's formula with the unit $H(1)$ (\dirn{K8EXACT20261106}; a separate clause checker confirms the dumped
assignments). The certified sixfold $54$-point set and its mirror satisfy every clause of both encoders' $9$-layer
formulas, with $Y(1,2)$ toggling (\dirn{C6C7REVIEW}); the $60$-point sets A and B of Section~\ref{sec:lower} satisfy
encoder~A's $10$-layer formula and every cut family produced on 5 November (\dirn{SIX60}).
\item \emph{Cross-encoder} (exact computation, through a shared literal-translation harness, so not independent): the
non-chain parts of A and B force the same orientation literals on all $185{,}549$ ($m=7$) and $11{,}738+23{,}852$
($m=6$, $9$ and $11$ layers) orbit--pattern pairs.
\item Chain clauses agree with brute force over all $8$-subsets on random $2$- and $3$-layer configurations ($880$
for encoder~B at $m=6$, no unsound or inexact case), and no non-chain clause is violated by random larger
configurations.
\item \emph{Calibration}: for $(m,K)=(3,4),(4,5),(5,6),(6,7)$ the encoding is satisfiable exactly at the known maximum
number of layers and unsatisfiable one layer beyond (the four unsatisfiable formulas were regenerated with matching
hashes, solved again and certified by \cakelpr{} on 5 November, \dirn{LRATCHECK20261105/recheck}).
\end{itemize}

\section{The certificates}\label{sec:cert}

\paragraph{Checkers.} All formulas were first solved by CaDiCaL~3.0.1 (commit \texttt{c6073042}) with text LRAT
output and checked by \cakelpr; the sixfold replay of 6 November used CaDiCaL~2.1.3 (Section~\ref{sec:c6}). A certificate is the line \texttt{s VERIFIED UNSAT} of \cakelpr{} for a specific CNF file and LRAT
file. The link from a certified file to the analysed programs is regeneration: fresh runs of the generators reproduce
the base formulas byte for byte, and the cube files are the base formula plus units, which is checked structurally and,
for all $64$ cube files, by hash (Section~\ref{sec:enc}, ``Validation''); the link to geometry is
Corollary~\ref{k8s:cor:geom}. \lratcheck{} also accepted every proof of the original runs (it was not used in the
replay of 6 November); by the defect described in Section~\ref{sec:defs} this is supporting information only. For the
review replays of 4 November the binaries had SHA-256 \texttt{e12ecc8c\dots} (CaDiCaL), \texttt{2fee767a\dots}
(\cakelpr) and \texttt{f2046212\dots} (\lratcheck) (\dirn{C6C7REVIEW/REPLAY.md}); for the sixfold replay of 6 November,
\texttt{4acf5860\dots} (CaDiCaL~2.1.3) and \texttt{c14ff498\dots} (\cakelpr)
(\dirn{C6UPPER/replay-2026-11-06/TOOLS_AND_PROOFS.sha256}). The replay thus used a different \cakelpr{} build from the one
used in the review of 4 November; building commit \texttt{033aad53} of the public \cakelpr{} repository
(\texttt{github.com/tanyongkiam/cake\_lpr}) with its Makefile on the same workstation reproduces it byte for byte
(\dirn{C6UPPER/replay-2026-11-06/README.md}).

\subsection{Sixfold}\label{sec:c6}

\paragraph{Split.} The base formula plus the unit $Y(1,2)$ is split into the $32$ sign patterns of
$Y(1,3)$, $Y(1,4)$, $Y(2,3)$, $Y(2,4)$, $Y(3,4)$ (Lemma~\ref{k8s:lem:cube}). Each cube file is the base formula, with adjusted
header, plus $Y(1,2)$ and the five literals of its pattern; that this holds for all $32$ files of each encoder and that the
patterns are distinct was checked by \dirn{C6UPPER/tools/verify_cover.py} and by the separately written
\dirn{C6C7REVIEW/strict_cover.py}, which also reject a missing cube, a changed clause, a flipped unit and a changed header
(exact computation). Twenty patterns contradict transitivity and are refuted at once (under $1$\,s each); the other twelve
are the orders of $\psi_1,\dots,\psi_4$ with $\psi_1<\psi_2$ (Table~\ref{tab:c6cert}).

\paragraph{Runs.} Encoder~A: one core per cube, $8$ lanes, $56$ minutes wall clock, about $20{,}000$ CPU seconds;

(heap $8{,}000$\,MB for A, $4{,}000$\,MB for B); the completion times in \dirn{C6UPPER/logs/cake.txt} and
\dirn{C6UPPER/logs/encb_cake.txt} span $31$ and $84$ minutes for the $32$ proofs of each encoder. An unsplit run of the
whole instance was stopped after $6{,}578$\,s without an answer; it proves nothing.

\paragraph{What has been replayed.} All $64$ cube proofs ($32$ per encoder) were accepted by \cakelpr{} when they were
produced, on 3 November (\dirn{C6UPPER/logs/cake.txt}, \dirn{C6UPPER/logs/encb_cake.txt}); those logs record cube labels,
not formula or proof hashes. On 4 November a review replayed three randomly chosen phase-order proofs per encoder
(marked $^\dagger$) with both checkers against freshly generated formulas, with matching hashes
(\dirn{C6C7REVIEW/REPLAY.md}), so, before the replay below, $6$ of the $64$ \cakelpr{} verdicts were bound to file
hashes; the same day all $64$
proofs, with hashes matching the recorded ones, were replayed against freshly generated formulas with \lratcheck{} only,
which is not a certificate (\dirn{C6UPPER/logs/replay_2026-11-04.txt}).

In the hash-bound \cakelpr{} replay of 6 November 2026 (\dirn{C6UPPER/replay-2026-11-06}) the following was done and
recorded, for each encoder:
\begin{itemize}
\item the base formula was regenerated, and its hash had to equal the record;
\item the $32$ cube files were rebuilt with \dirn{mkcubes.py}, and \dirn{verify_cover.py} reported a complete cover;
\item the hash of each cube file was compared with its record in \dirn{C6UPPER/SHA256SUMS.txt} before any solving, and
all $64$ matched.
\end{itemize}
Each cube formula was then solved again with CaDiCaL~2.1.3, the SHA-256 of the fresh proof was recorded, and the proof
was checked by \cakelpr. Every solver run ended UNSAT, and all $64$ proofs were accepted (\texttt{s VERIFIED UNSAT});
none was rejected. Each verdict is recorded together with the hashes of its formula and proof
(\dirn{results.tsv}), and an independent check of that record confirmed the hashes and verdict lines.
\begin{itemize}
\item The $40$ fresh proofs of the contradictory cubes are byte-identical to the archived ones.
\item The $24$ fresh phase-order proofs differ from those of Table~\ref{tab:c6cert}; for these formulas the certificate
is the fresh proof.
\end{itemize}
The run took $63{,}539$\,s of CaDiCaL wall time, first on one lane and then on six. The accepted proofs are kept
compressed ($28.4$\,GB, outside the repository, not public).

\subsection{The upper bounds}

\begin{theorem}[upper bounds; certificates, two encoders, each verdict bound to formula and proof hashes: for $m=7$ by
the replay of 4 November, for $m=6$ by the hash-bound \cakelpr{} replay of 6 November ($64$ of $64$ cube formulas); on
top of the written soundness proof (not refereed) of Section~\ref{k8s:sec} and the Lean-checked
reduction of Proposition~\ref{prop:reduction}]\label{thm:upper}
\lean{Sevenfold70} and \lean{Sixfold66} hold. Hence every sevenfold rotationally symmetric set of at least $65$ points in
general position, and every sixfold one of at least $61$ points, contains $8$ points in convex position.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By Table~\ref{tab:c7cert}, $F_A(7,8,10)$ plus $H(1)$ and $F_B(7,8,10)$ are unsatisfiable (certificates); by
Corollary~\ref{k8s:cor:geom}(b), \lean{Sevenfold70} holds. By the replay of 6 November (Section~\ref{sec:c6}, ``What
has been replayed''), for each encoder all $32$ formulas ``base $(6,8,11)$ $+\,Y(1,2)$ $+$ cube'' are unsatisfiable
(certificates); by Corollary~\ref{k8s:cor:geom}(a), \lean{Sixfold66} holds. Proposition~\ref{prop:reduction} gives the rest. One
encoder suffices in each case; the second is a cross-check.
\end{proof}

\section{The lower-bound constructions}\label{sec:lower}

\begin{theorem}[exact computation]\label{thm:lower}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item The five files \dirn{SIX60/sets/c6_60pts_X.pts}, where $X$ is one of A, B, C, C2 and D,
describe sixfold symmetric sets of $60$ points (ten orbits, no centre) in general position without $8$ points in convex
position, of five pairwise different order types (called A, B, C, C$'$, D).
\item The eight files of \dirn{PRIMEFOLD/sets/k8} describe sevenfold symmetric sets of $64$ points (the centre and nine
orbits) in general position without $8$ points in convex position, of seven pairwise different order types
(\dirn{p7_compound_64} and \dirn{p7_two_orbit_64} have the same orientation table).
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\paragraph{Format.} Each file lists one point per line as integers $(w_0,\dots,w_{m-1})$ for the point
$\sum_jw_j\zeta^j$, $\zeta=e^{2\pi i/m}$. Multiplication by $\zeta$ is a cyclic shift of this vector, so the symmetry is
exact. Every orbit is $\{\zeta^js:0\le j<m\}$ for a \emph{seed} $s$. In every file the rows other than the centre are
distinct and split into orbits of exactly $m$ rows, each consisting of the $m$ cyclic shifts of its first row in the
file, which we take as its seed; in all files except the three cluster files \dirn{p7_compound_64},
\dirn{p7_two_orbit_64} and \dirn{m7_x2_G9s_centre}, whose rows are listed cluster by cluster, the orbits are consecutive
blocks of $m$ rows. This, and the hash of every file against \dirn{SIX60/sets/SHA256SUMS.txt} and
\dirn{PRIMEFOLD/SHA256SUMS}, is checked by \dirn{WRITEUP/P1/tools/make_tables.py}. For $m=6$ every point is $a+b\zeta$ with integers $a,b$, i.e.\ a point of the
hexagonal lattice; the linear map $a+b\zeta\mapsto(a,b)$ has positive determinant, so all orientation signs are signs of
integer determinants. For $m=7$ the signs are signs of elements of $\mathbb Z[\zeta_7]$, decided exactly. Two examples
with small coordinates, as seeds $(a,b)$ for $a+b\zeta$:
\begin{description}[font=\normalfont\itshape,leftmargin=1.5em,style=nextline]
\input{tables/seed_c6_60pts_D}
\input{tables/seed_c7_64pts_small}
\end{description}
Appendix~\ref{app:seeds} lists the seeds of all thirteen files, with the number of digits of the largest coefficient of
each file (from $3$ for \dirn{c7_64pts_small} to $31$ for \dirn{m7_x2_G9s_centre}).

\paragraph{How the sets were found} (the claims rest only on the exact checks below).
\emph{Sixfold} (\dirn{SIX60/construction}). Sets A and B were found by \emph{alternating projections}: starting from a
real $10$-layer configuration with few convex octagons ($90$ in the best start), a SAT solver on encoder~A's formula,
together with all cut clauses produced earlier, was steered towards that configuration's orientation signs, real
configurations were fitted to the resulting abstract models, and local annealing on the exact number of convex octagons
drove it to $0$; the coordinates were then made exact in $\mathbb Z[\zeta_6]$. Set C was found independently by a
\emph{phase-fixed LP-CEGAR} loop: with the phases fixed, every orientation is the sign of a linear form in the inverse
radii, so existence of radii for a sign vector is a linear program, and each infeasible sign vector yields a Farkas
clause; after $2{,}284$ SAT/LP rounds one perturbed phase vector gave a realizable octagon-free sign vector (LP margin
$9.3\cdot10^{-4}$). C$'$ is C rounded at scale $10^9$ (its own exact check gives a different order type), and D is A
after a constrained local optimisation that keeps the octagon count $0$ and raises the smallest normalized sine from
$2.2\cdot10^{-5}$ to $1.3\cdot10^{-3}$, with coefficients at most $2^{19}$. The shapes differ: A is a spiral of near-twin
layers, B and C have needles of eight layers near the midpoints of the outer edges.
\emph{Sevenfold} (\dirn{PRIMEFOLD}~\S3, \dirn{ES8SYM}~\S6). Four sets come from simulated annealing of layer radii and
phases with exact rounding (two annealers, each rounded at two scales); \dirn{p7_compound_64} is one orbit of a
two-level $9$-point cluster, \dirn{rule_p7_64pts} comes from an explicit cluster rule, and \dirn{m7_x2_G9s_centre} is one
orbit of chord-aligned flat $9$-point clusters, each with the centre.

\paragraph{Verification} (exact computation).
\emph{Sixfold}: each set was checked by three separately written implementations (\dirn{SIX60/README.md}, section ``Verification''):
(i)~the pipeline of \dirn{ES8SYM/tools} (\dirn{verify_cfg.py}: exact algebraic signs and, separately, interval
arithmetic; \dirn{cvx2.c}: two differently anchored dynamic programs for convex subsets; \dirn{cvxcheck.c}: depth-first
search; \dirn{crosscheck_decimal.py}; \dirn{enum_convex.c}), run by the finders, and for C and C$'$ also the separate
checker \dirn{indep_check.py}; (ii)~\dirn{SIX60/verify/verify60.py}, standard library only, in the oblique integer
coordinates: distinctness, absence of the origin, closure under $(a,b)\mapsto(-b,a+b)$, all $34{,}220$ triples
non-collinear, and the largest convex subset by two independently anchored $O(n^4)$ dynamic programs (validated against
brute force on $150$ random small sets and on planted convex $9$-gons); (iii)~\dirn{SIX60/verify/dfs_convex.c}, an
exhaustive depth-first enumeration of all subsets in convex position with exact \verb|__int128| orientations.
\emph{Sevenfold}: \dirn{PRIMEFOLD/check64} (written for an independent check) verifies distinctness, exact $7$-fold
invariance and all $41{,}664$ orientation signs exactly in $\mathbb Z[\zeta_7]$ (and again with $110$-digit decimals), and
counts convex $k$-subsets by an anchored dynamic program and again by a separate C enumerator working on the sign table;
the five files that are also in \dirn{ES8SYM/sets} were checked by the \dirn{ES8SYM} pipeline as well;
\dirn{K8EXACT20261106} recomputed all orientation signs of all eight files with a separately written $\mathbb Z[\zeta_7]$ sign
routine and found agreement with \dirn{PRIMEFOLD/check64/z7exact.py}. So every sevenfold
convex-subset count rests on at least two separately written programs, and on four or more for the five \dirn{ES8SYM}
files.

\paragraph{Order types.} The numbers of convex $k$-subsets do not change under relabelling or reflection. The counts of
convex $4$-subsets in Tables~\ref{tab:counts6} and~\ref{tab:counts7} are pairwise different within each table, so the
sets of each part of Theorem~\ref{thm:lower} have pairwise different order types, also up to reflection. The classical
Erd\H{o}s--Szekeres $64$-point set has $422{,}186$ convex $4$-subsets and no non-trivial automorphism, so it is not
order-type equivalent to any set with a rotation or reflection symmetry (exact computation, \dirn{ES8SYM}~\S6).
Clusters of blow-ups in the sense of Baek and Balko~\cite{BB25} are line-modules, an order-type invariant (written
lemma, not refereed, \dirn{ES8SYM/proofs/structure.md}). So the following excludes order-type equivalence to such
blow-ups with clusters of the stated sizes (exact computation): \dirn{c7_64pts_small} and \dirn{c7_64pts_9layers_centre}
have no line-module with $2$ to $60$ points, \dirn{c7_64pts_9layers_centre_own} none with $2$ to $56$ (\dirn{ES8SYM}~\S6,
\dirn{PRIMEFOLD/check64/modules60}), and \dirn{c7_64_own_s1000} none with $2$ to $20$
(\dirn{PRIMEFOLD/check64/check64.log}; larger modules were not checked for it). The last three sets of
Table~\ref{tab:counts7} are built from $9$-point clusters and do have line-modules, among them seven of size $9$
(\dirn{check64.log}); whether they are equivalent to blow-ups was not checked.

\paragraph{Consistency with the encodings.} As stated in Section~\ref{sec:enc}, the sevenfold sets and their mirrors,
without the centre, satisfy both encoders' $9$-layer formulas (exact computation, \dirn{K8EXACT20261106}), and the
sixfold set A, labelled by encoder~A's convention, gives an assignment of all $5{,}710$ orbit signs and the phase-order
variables that extends to a model of encoder~A's $10$-layer formula and satisfies all $2{,}157{,}010$ clauses of the $74$
cut files produced on 5 November (exact computation, \dirn{SIX60}). A real configuration satisfies every sound clause, so
these are consistency checks of the encodings and of the cuts; they are not part of the proof.

\begin{remark}[history of the sixfold value]\label{rem:history}
Until 5 November the largest sixfold octagon-free set known to us had $54$ points, and in our records the sixfold
maximum was either $54$ or $60$. The plain encoding is satisfiable at $10$ layers, and abstract $10$-layer models satisfying all $3$-term
Grassmann--Pl\"ucker relations had resisted realization (evidence only, \dirn{ROT456}~\S3); several of them were
excluded one at a time for the prescribed sixfold rotation (written proofs, not refereed, with identities checked by exact
computation; \dirn{C6C7REVIEW}, \dirn{ROTREFINE20261104}). The question was settled by construction. Since set A lies in
the phase-order cube $\psi_1<\psi_2<\psi_3<\psi_4$, that $10$-layer cube could never have become unsatisfiable.
\end{remark}

\paragraph{What is trusted.} The Lean~4 kernel and the Mathlib definitions used in the statements; \cakelpr{} and the
machine that ran it; the Python interpreter, to run the generators as written; SHA-256, to identify files; and the
reading of the generator sources on which the code-to-clause correspondence rests (gap~(G1)). No step from a DIMACS file
to \lean{Sixfold66} or \lean{Sevenfold70} is formalized (gap~(G2)).

\paragraph{Further limitations.} (1)~The proof files ($1.7$\,GB and $1.6$\,GB for $m=7$; $41.0$\,GB and $46.5$\,GB for
$m=6$) are in local archives (\dirn{es8-c7-octagon-2026-11-03}, \dirn{es8-c6-octagon-2026-11-03},
\dirn{es8-c6c7-review-2026-11-04}) and are not public, and so are the proofs of the sixfold replay of 6 November
($28.4$\,GB compressed); no public deposit with a DOI exists yet. The formulas can be regenerated, and solved and checked
again, with the commands of Section~\ref{sec:repro} (a new solver run need not reproduce the same proof file; in the
replay of 6 November, with CaDiCaL~2.1.3, $24$ of the $64$ proofs differed from the archived ones). (2)~Some program comments in \dirn{C7UPPER/gen_b.py} and the angular docstring of
\dirn{C7UPPER/gen.py} still state chain implications in the reverse direction, and that docstring omits the antipodal
case of Section~\ref{k8s:sec:antipodal}; the emitted formulas are unaffected (documentation only). (3)~Nothing has been
refereed.

\section{Reproducibility}\label{sec:repro}

All commands run from \dirn{cloud/es7-2026-10-19/results}; tool locations are passed as environment variables.

\paragraph{Lean.} From the repository root (dependencies prebuilt; $23$\,s and $2.6$\,GB on 6 November):
{\footnotesize
\begin{verbatim}
lake env lean cloud/es7-2026-10-19/results/LAYERLEAN/LayerLemma.lean
\end{verbatim}}

\paragraph{Sevenfold formulas and proofs.}
{\footnotesize
\begin{verbatim}
python3 C7UPPER/gen.py 7 8 10 m7K8t10.cnf                # sha 1a7c0e70...; meta file names H(1) = var 7857
python3 C7UPPER/addunits.py m7K8t10.cnf m7K8t10_H1.cnf 7857   # appends H(1): sha fa297b5b...
python3 C6UPPER/encb/gen_b2.py 7 8 10 B_m7K8t10.cnf      # sha b4d29017... (= C7UPPER/gen_b.py output)
cadical --lrat --binary=false <cnf> <proof.lrat>         # CaDiCaL 3.0.1
cake_lpr --CML_HEAP_SIZE=8000 <cnf> <proof.lrat>         # must print: s VERIFIED UNSAT
S=<dir with resolve/bin/{cadical,lrat-check}> bash C7UPPER/repro.sh [solve]
\end{verbatim}}
\noindent\dirn{C7UPPER/repro.sh} runs the validation suite (about $90$\,s) and, with \texttt{solve}, re-solves; its own
proof check uses \lratcheck, so \cakelpr{} must be run separately.

\paragraph{Sixfold formulas, cubes and proofs.}
{\footnotesize
\begin{verbatim}
python3 C7UPPER/gen.py 6 8 11 m6K8t11.cnf                               # A: sha 542c8a3a...
python3 C6UPPER/tools/mkcubes.py m6K8t11.cnf m6K8t11.cnf.json cubes     # full_Y12.cnf + 32 cubes
python3 C6UPPER/tools/verify_cover.py m6K8t11.cnf m6K8t11.cnf.json cubes
python3 C6UPPER/encb/gen_b2.py 6 8 11 B_m6K8t11.cnf                     # B: sha 479e31a9...

P=<work dir> S=<dir with resolve/bin> python3 C6UPPER/tools/run.py 8 <deadline>   # CaDiCaL lanes
P=<work dir> S=<dir with resolve/bin> bash C6UPPER/tools/cake.sh                  # cake_lpr, one at a time
python3 -I C6C7REVIEW/replay.py --seed 1319527528443935447 ...          # the 4 November sampled replay

python3 replay.py          # first set R, CAKE, CAD at the top; or: LANES=6 python3 replay_par.py

\section{Open problems}\label{sec:open}

\paragraph{The other rotation orders at $k=8$} (Table~\ref{tab:status}). By the layer lemma, a counterexample to
$ES(8)=65$ with fivefold symmetry needs $13$ layers ($65$ points, with or without centre), and one with fourfold symmetry
$17$ layers ($68$ points). The encodings of Section~\ref{sec:enc} apply unchanged, but the threshold formulas have not
been refuted. The following is evidence only; timed-out runs prove nothing. For $m=5$, splitting by the $64$ sign
patterns of $Y(1,2),\dots,Y(3,4)$ with the unit $H(1)$ refutes the $40$ patterns that contradict transitivity at once,
but phase-order cubes ran for up to $22{,}102$\,s (about $5\cdot10^7$ conflicts, against $2.0$--$2.6\cdot10^6$ for the
sixfold cubes) without an answer (\dirn{ROT456}~\S4). Runs of 5 November with additional clauses from a chord lemma
(written proof, not refereed; each added clause checked by exact computation; \dirn{CHORD20261105}) refuted the impossible
patterns again, with proofs accepted by \cakelpr, but closed none of the $24$ fivefold phase orders ($19$ ran for up to
about $15$ hours, $5$ were never started) and none of the $12$ fourfold ones (about $15$ hours; one run was lost)
(\dirn{ROT45CHORD20261105}). At $14$ fourfold layers an abstract model consistent with all $3$-term
Grassmann--Pl\"ucker (GP) relations exists and has not been realized (\dirn{ROT456}~\S3). The plain fivefold encoding is
satisfiable at $12$ layers; after lazy GP refinement a GP-consistent $12$-layer model was found and then excluded for the
prescribed fivefold rotation by an exact linear identity over $\mathbb Q(\sqrt5)$ (written proof, not refereed, with the identity checked by exact
computation; \dirn{ROTREFINE20261104}). With such identities added the $12$-layer formula stayed satisfiable, by models
that are not GP-consistent, and the refined $13$-layer formula gave no answer in $600$\,s (\dirn{ROTREFINE20261104}).
\emph{Is every fivefold symmetric set of $65$ points, and every fourfold one of $68$ points, in
general position forced to contain $8$ points in convex position?}

\paragraph{Threefold symmetry.} Here $8>2\cdot3$ and the layer lemma does not apply. Every convex layer is a triangle, a
hexagon or the centre (written proof, not refereed, \dirn{ES8SYM}~\S3), and since $3\cdot21+1<65$, a threefold
counterexample to $ES(8)=65$ exists if and only if some threefold set of $22$ orbits without centre is octagon-free.
The largest known threefold octagon-free sets have $61$ points; a threefold $64$-point set and its $63$-point subset
without the centre each have exactly three convex octagons (exact computation, \dirn{ES8SYM}). A radius-ordered
relaxation of the encoding without nesting clauses (written soundness argument, not refereed, \dirn{C6C7REVIEW},
\dirn{THREEFOLDRELAX}) was implemented as \dirn{THREEFOLDRELAX/gen_relax.py} with the option \texttt{--nonest} and
validated on the known threefold sets (exact computation). It is too weak (evidence only): for $K=7$ it stays
satisfiable at $10$, $11$, $12$ and $13$ orbits, although threefold sets without $7$ points in convex position have at
most $10$ orbits (computer-assisted: the threefold $33$-point statement \lean{Threefold33} of \dirn{SYMLEAN}, certified
in \dirn{C3FINAL}), and the threshold formula
$(3,8,22)$, with $170{,}270$ variables and $7{,}400{,}332$ clauses, gave no answer in $800$\,s.

\paragraph{The half-turn.} Does every centrally symmetric set of $66$ points in general position contain $8$ points in
convex position? $64$-point examples without one exist (Section~\ref{sec:related}).

\paragraph{Larger $k$.} SMQH's suspicion~\cite[\S7]{SMQH25} asks for symmetric extremal sets for all $k\ge7$. For
$(k-1)$-fold symmetry the size $2^{k-2}$ is possible only if $k-1$ is a power of $2$, an odd prime or an odd base-$2$
Fermat pseudoprime (orbit counting; core Lean-checked in \dirn{PRIMEFOLD/compat}); for $k=8$ the sevenfold sets above attain it. For $k=9$ the largest eightfold set
without $9$ points in convex position that we know has $120$ of the $128$ points that $ES(9)=129$ would allow
(\dirn{PRIMEFOLD}~\S5; exact computation).

\paragraph{Formalization.} Closing gaps (G1) and (G2) would need a verified encoder, or a Lean proof that the emitted
clauses are satisfied by every real configuration, together with a verified link from \cakelpr{} verdicts to Lean
propositions; the encoding of the empty hexagon theorem was verified in Lean in this spirit~\cite{SNGCCH24}.

\section{Seeds of the point sets}\label{app:seeds}

Each set is the union of the orbits $\{\zeta^js:0\le j<m\}$ of the listed seeds $s$, written as coefficient vectors
$(w_0,w_1,\dots)$ of $\sum_jw_j\zeta^j$ with trailing zeros omitted, plus the centre for $m=7$. Coordinates are scaled
integers; only orientations matter. The listing is generated from the files by \dirn{WRITEUP/P1/tools/make_tables.py},
which checks the hashes and that the rows other than the centre are exactly the $m$ cyclic shifts of the listed seeds
(the seed of an orbit is its first row in the file).
